Infrastructure, with a reason

Auth retains MySQL from Jobber; Users retains MongoDB. PostgreSQL owns the proposed transactional grocery domains. Your example illustrates flow; it does not require moving both Auth and Users to PostgreSQL. All 16 services use TypeScript + Node.js; no separate Email or Audit microservice is added here. Notification handles email/SMS/FCM; domain services own durable audit records.

Service boundaries

Auth → MySQL. Users, Catalog, Cart, Chat, Notification and Support → MongoDB. Store, Inventory, Order, Payment, Delivery, Review, Growth and Platform → PostgreSQL.

Within one SQL owner, retain useful foreign keys and transactions. Across services, keep stable IDs and validate through owner APIs/events; do not create cross-database foreign keys.

Conversion rules

Preserve legacy IDs, decimal precision, nullable values and timestamps. MongoDB collection structure is designed per aggregate; SQL tables are not automatically copied one-to-one. Redis keys and Elasticsearch indices are separate from the authoritative databases.

Users is explicitly split between identity and profile ownership. Laravel queue/cache/updater tables need replacement decisions rather than direct ports.

All model relationships, casts and field rules

Model methods can add casts, accessors and relationships beyond migration columns. Full model source is included. Relationship methods do not themselves prove a database foreign-key constraint.
